name: Strait of Hormuz
analysis: The most critical oil and LNG chokepoint. Most of what crossed it went to Asia, and bypass pipelines can carry only part of the crude.
situation: Largely blocked by Iran since late February 2026; traffic is close to a standstill.

name: Strait of Malacca
analysis: The largest oil chokepoint by volume, linking Middle East suppliers with East and Southeast Asia, and a major LNG route.

name: Suez Canal & SUMED pipeline
analysis: Oil and LNG through Suez collapsed after Houthi attacks in the Red Sea pushed ships around the Cape.

name: Bab el-Mandeb Strait
analysis: The gate between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Oil traffic roughly halved and LNG traffic all but disappeared after the Red Sea attacks.
situation: In July 2026 the Houthis declared a blockade of Saudi Arabia, turning Saudi tankers away from the strait.

name: Cape of Good Hope
analysis: Oil and LNG around the Cape rose sharply once ships started avoiding the Red Sea.

name: Panama Canal
analysis: A small share of world oil flows, almost all refined products, plus LNG from the US Gulf Coast to Asia and western South America.

name: Turkish Straits (Bosporus & Dardanelles)
analysis: The only outlet of the Black Sea for oil from Russia and the Caspian region, and for Ukrainian and Russian grain. Kazakhstan is the largest oil exporter through it.

name: Danish Straits
analysis: The exit from the Baltic. Russia remains its largest oil shipper, sending most volumes to Asia and Türkiye.

name: Lombok Strait
analysis: An alternative to Malacca through the Indonesian archipelago. No sourced traffic volume is available.

name: Sunda Strait
analysis: An alternative to Malacca between Java and Sumatra. No sourced traffic volume is available.
